actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: The repository provides simulation and learning environments for the OpenArm robotic platform, built on NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab
Isaac Lab training environments cover reach, lift a cube and open a drawer
The repository has been tested with Ubuntu 22.04, Isaac Sim v5.1.0, Isaac Lab v2.3.0 and Python 3.11
The package is installed with python -m pip install -e source/openarm
Teleoperation and sim-to-sim/sim-to-real transfer pipelines are under development
The unimanual reach task is registered with the gym id Isaac-Reach-OpenArm-v0
The entry_point of Isaac-Reach-OpenArm-v0 is isaaclab.envs:ManagerBasedRLEnv, a class outside this repository
The env_cfg_entry_point of Isaac-Reach-OpenArm-v0 is joint_pos_env_cfg:OpenArmReachEnvCfg
OpenArmReachEnvCfg subclasses ReachEnvCfg and switches the scene robot to the unimanual OpenArm configuration
The reach configuration sets a JointPositionActionCfg over openarm_joint.* with scale 0.5 and use_default_offset True as its arm action
The reach control step is two physics steps (decimation 2) and the physics timestep is 1/60 s
The reach episode is 12.0 s long
The policy observation group concatenates the joint_pos, joint_vel, pose_command and actions terms
The joint_pos and joint_vel observation terms read the seven joints openarm_joint1 to openarm_joint7
The pose command is sampled in pos_x 0.25 to 0.35, pos_y -0.2 to 0.2, pos_z 0.3 to 0.4, roll -pi/6 to pi/6, pitch pi/2 and yaw -pi/9 to pi/9
The pose command is resampled every 4 s
The joint_pos and joint_vel observations add uniform noise between -0.01 and 0.01
The default scene holds 4096 parallel environments
The robot asset declares velocity limits 2.175 for openarm_joint1 to openarm_joint4 and 2.61 for openarm_joint5 to openarm_joint7, and effort limits 40.0, 27.0 and 7.0 by joint group

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the fake's random generator and its integration is deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the fake was never compared with a run of the Isaac Lab environment

gaps: the fake is an interface stand-in, not Isaac Lab: it has no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, USD scene, sensors or reward terms, and was never compared with a run of Isaac-Reach-OpenArm-v0

the action and observation spaces are placeholders: the fake exposes seven unbounded joint-position offsets and a 28-value observation, while the upstream spaces, their bounds and the observation scaling are built by Isaac Lab outside this clone; the package therefore publishes no action limit
no vectorisation: the upstream scene defaults to 4096 environments (reach_env_cfg.py:254); the fake is one world
the real environment needs Isaac Sim 5.1.0 and Isaac Lab 2.3.0 on Linux with a GPU (README.md:19-23); the fake backend needs neither
no rendering and no snapshot or restore: the fake exposes no get_state/set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the world state is kept and stays readable
